test.name: A bounded ask reads what is already attached instead of searching for it
test.description: Issue #2813 item 4: "Before any search, read the person's attached sources and relatives. Never search for a record that is already attached." Cornelius Driscoll already has SD-DRIS-D, a Quebec civil death registration, among seven attached sources, so a request for a death record is a request for something the project already holds. The correct turn reads (person_read / source_attachments) and reports what is there; searching for it -- by an MCP search call or by handing off to a search step -- is the failure, because it is a paid call that returns what the project already had. GRADING: deterministic. The `attached-first` tag fires test_reads_attachments_before_searching, which reads the MCP call log and the hand-off list rather than the reply, so a turn that only NARRATES having checked cannot pass. This is the gap the unit suite could not previously reach: neither person_read nor source_attachments is in mock_mcp.LIVE_TOOLS, so the mock registers them only for a test that declares fixtures -- which this one does.

judge_context: This is a BOUNDED-REQUEST test about not re-finding what is already attached.

Cornelius Driscoll already has a Quebec civil death registration attached (SD-DRIS-D). The reply should say the death record is already attached and identify it. The hand-off and search behaviour is asserted deterministically, so do NOT grade routing; grade only whether the reply tells the researcher what is already there rather than announcing a search.
Do not grade citation formatting or source quality. This turn is a lookup, not an evaluation.
